task_2.title: Raise virtualenv minimum for safer poetry shell
task_2.description: The 1.8.4 update requires virtualenv 20.26.6 or newer so that environments created or entered through poetry shell benefit from the upstream mitigation for a potential command injection issue in untrusted projects.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that running poetry shell in untrusted projects is protected by requiring a virtualenv version that includes the upstream command injection mitigation.

expectation.grounded: The package metadata and dependency resolution for Poetry 1.8.4 must require virtualenv version 20.26.6 or newer. Installations or upgrades must not resolve Poetry with an older virtualenv release, and poetry shell should operate using a virtualenv release that contains the security mitigation referenced for PR #9757.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading to 1.8.4 should automatically receive a safe minimum virtual environment backend version, reducing command injection exposure when opening a Poetry-managed shell in projects they do not trust.

constraints.grounded: Do not relax the virtualenv lower bound below 20.26.6 for the 1.8.4 release. Preserve the existing poetry shell user workflow and avoid introducing unrelated command behavior changes beyond enforcing the safer virtualenv dependency floor.
constraints.conceptual: The update should harden dependency safety without changing how users invoke or interact with Poetry shell sessions.

behavior: Poetry 1.8.4 declares virtualenv 20.26.6 as the minimum acceptable virtualenv dependency version.
Dependency resolution for Poetry 1.8.4 excludes virtualenv releases older than 20.26.6.
When poetry shell is used after the upgrade, it runs with a virtualenv version that includes the upstream mitigation for the potential command injection vulnerability in untrusted projects.
No additional production behavior changes are evidenced by the provided code diff beyond the release-level virtualenv dependency requirement.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry 1.8.4 is installed or upgraded, the resolved virtualenv dependency should be version 20.26.6 or newer.
When an environment attempts to satisfy Poetry 1.8.4 with virtualenv older than 20.26.6, dependency resolution should reject that combination.
When a user runs poetry shell in an untrusted project after upgrading to 1.8.4, the command should rely on a virtualenv release containing the command injection mitigation.
Existing poetry shell invocation semantics should remain unchanged for users apart from the safer virtualenv dependency requirement.

task_1.title: Official Python 3.13 Support
task_1.description: Version 1.8.4 extends the library's officially supported Python runtime coverage to include Python 3.13. The provided production code diff does not show any public API, command, error-handling, or data model behavior changes, so the upgrade is a compatibility support change rather than a feature with new user-facing workflows.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the library officially supports use on Python 3.13 while preserving the existing behavior users rely on from version 1.8.3.

expectation.grounded: Python 3.13 must be treated as an officially supported interpreter for version 1.8.4. Existing public commands, APIs, return behavior, raised error types, warnings, and persisted state semantics should remain consistent with version 1.8.3 because the provided production diff contains no evidence of intentional runtime behavior changes beyond interpreter support.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to adopt Python 3.13 as a supported runtime without learning new commands, changing their existing workflows, or encountering intentional behavior changes unrelated to interpreter compatibility.

constraints.grounded: Do not narrow support for previously supported Python versions, change public command or API contracts, add new required user configuration, or alter observable outputs solely as part of adding Python 3.13 support. The update should not introduce new user-visible features beyond the expanded interpreter support.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should be compatibility-preserving: it broadens where the library can run, but should not change what users can do or how existing functionality behaves.

behavior: Python 3.13 is now included in the officially supported runtime set for version 1.8.4.
Running the library under Python 3.13 should be considered supported rather than experimental or unsupported.
No new public APIs, commands, options, return values, warnings, error types, or persisted state changes are evidenced by the provided production code diff.
Existing behavior from version 1.8.3 should remain stable across already supported Python runtimes.
acceptance_criteria: When a user installs or runs version 1.8.4 with Python 3.13, it should be treated as a supported runtime environment.
When users perform existing workflows on Python 3.13, those workflows should behave consistently with the same workflows on previously supported Python versions.
When users upgrade from version 1.8.3 to 1.8.4 on an already supported Python version, they should not need to change commands, configuration, or API usage because of this update.
When existing public APIs or commands are invoked after the upgrade, they should not expose new warnings, errors, or output changes solely due to the Python 3.13 support addition.

task_3.title: Recognize Python 3.13
task_3.description: Poetry Core's known Python version lists were extended to include Python 3.13 so generated package metadata and Python constraint formatting treat Python 3.13 as an available interpreter version.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Poetry Core recognizes Python 3.13 as an available Python version wherever it derives package Python classifiers or formats Python version constraints from its known-version list.

expectation.grounded: The public known-version sets used by Package.AVAILABLE_PYTHONS and the version-helper PYTHON_VERSION list must include Python 3.13, represented consistently with the surrounding minor versions. Package.all_classifiers should produce the Python 3.13 classifier when the package's python_versions constraint allows Python 3.13, and format_python_constraint should evaluate Python 3.13.* when summarizing supported or excluded Python ranges.
expectation.conceptual: Projects that support Python 3.13 should receive the same automatic metadata and constraint-handling behavior already provided for earlier recognized Python versions.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove or change recognition of the existing supported Python versions from 2.x through 3.12. Do not alter the semantics of version constraint parsing, classifier de-duplication, or classifier ordering except for adding Python 3.13 where the existing algorithms determine it is allowed.
constraints.conceptual: The update should be additive and backward compatible: existing package metadata and Python constraint behavior should remain unchanged unless Python 3.13 is relevant to the package's declared support range.

behavior: Python 3.13 is treated as a known available Python version for package-level Python classifier generation.
Python 3.13.* is included in the known Python minor-version universe used when formatting Python version constraints.
When a package declares a Python version constraint that allows Python 3.13, automatically generated classifiers include Python 3.13 alongside the other allowed Python versions.
When a formatted Python constraint is computed, Python 3.13 is considered during the same allow/exclude evaluation as the other known Python minor versions.
acceptance_criteria: Given a package whose declared Python support includes Python 3.13, when its complete classifier list is generated, then the resulting metadata should include a Python 3.13 classifier.
Given a package whose declared Python support excludes Python 3.13, when its complete classifier list is generated, then Python 3.13 should not be added solely because it is known.

When Python version constraints are formatted through the public helper behavior, Python 3.13.* should participate in the accepted and excluded version calculations just like adjacent known Python minor versions.

When existing projects target Python versions earlier than 3.13, their generated classifiers and formatted constraints should remain compatible with the previous behavior except where their constraints also include Python 3.13.
